cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: You Handle the Impossible Part
cards.instruction: Make someone accept responsibility for the one part of the plan that cannot reasonably be done.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Payroll needs yesterday's missing hour. You get it into this jar; I'll label it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How can an hour fit through that opening?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take the lid off first. Don't diagnose a capacity problem while the container's closed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've got both hands free. You catch it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I need them free to record the precise recovery time. Tell me the moment you've caught it; please don't make my record approximate.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 corrects capacity diagnosis and A5 demands precise documentation, using expert recordkeeping to reserve ordinary work and keep B catching the impossible hour.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 opening objection causes lid correction; B4 free-hands challenge gets an explicit answer reserving them for timing records.

relationship.evidence: B2 challenges feasibility and B4 offers A the same work, a credible refusal of an unequal division.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 hands argument to defend A's labeling role and pin the exact recovery report on B.

specificity.evidence: A1 payroll, missing hour and jar establish the reason for the strange assignment.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 now directly answers whose hands are free; the precise-time request makes the refusal playable without the prior dangling fragment.
